Analysis modes

SpPrAn 0.3.0 provides two user-facing choices in the Configuration Builder: Supervised and Unsupervised. A third configuration value, full, is used when optional full phenotype discovery is enabled.

Supervised mode

type_of_analysis: supervised

Supervised mode is hypothesis-driven. Users define major cell types and, optionally, nested subtypes using protein-marker positivity rules.

Use this mode when the protein marker combinations defining the populations of interest are known in advance.

The workflow includes:

  • primary cell-type annotation;

  • hierarchical subtype annotation;

  • cell counts and proportions;

  • phenotype-hierarchy outputs; and

  • spatial overview, highlight, or custom plots.

Unsupervised mode

type_of_analysis: unsupervised

Unsupervised mode keeps major cell types user-defined, but discovers subphenotypes from observed combinations of selected exploratory protein markers within one or more of those parent populations.

The term unsupervised does not mean that all cells are clustered without prior biological information. Parent populations remain protein-marker-rule-defined. The exploratory step enumerates observed binary protein marker patterns within them.

The workflow can generate:

  • sample-by-cell-type proportion matrices;

  • optional sample-level pie plots;

  • observed phenotype labels and protein-marker-pattern mappings;

  • phenotype proportions within selected parent populations;

  • optional two-group phenotype comparisons; and

  • optional protein-marker intensity summaries.

Two-group comparison

Samples can optionally be assigned to two groups, such as Control and Treatment. For phenotypes found in both groups, SpPrAn can report descriptive summaries and perform:

  • two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests;

  • Welch independent-samples t-tests; and

  • Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction.

Group-specific phenotypes are also reported.

Caution

Statistical significance should be interpreted together with biological sample size, phenotype-detection frequency, effect magnitude, multiple-test correction, and experimental design.

Marker-intensity summaries

Selected protein-marker intensities can be summarized within discovered phenotypes. SpPrAn exports Tukey-style box-plot summary values and outliers for downstream visualization.

Full phenotype discovery

type_of_analysis: full

The Configuration Builder exposes full phenotype discovery as an option in the unsupervised workflow.

Full mode:

  1. runs unsupervised protein-marker-pattern discovery;

  2. combines the observed phenotype definitions across samples;

  3. converts those protein marker patterns into SpPrAn subtype definitions;

  4. regenerates annotated AnnData objects; and

  5. continues through the supervised workflow.

Caution

If the total of discovered phenotypes for a cell type is higher than 512, they will be omitted from the supervised analysis.

Biological interpretation

A discovered phenotype is an observed combination of protein marker positivity states within a defined parent population. It is not automatically a distinct cell lineage, differentiation state, or functional state.

Interpret the phenotype using the tissue context and the known specificity and function of the protein markers in the panel.
